NovaExplorer — Their Missions Ended. Their Stories Didn't.

What happens to a spacecraft after its mission ends? Its operations may stop, but its discoveries continue to shape our understanding of space.

NovaExplorer is a gamified educational web platform that brings the stories of retired and abandoned NASA spacecraft back to life. Designed for young space enthusiasts, it transforms authentic NASA mission histories, images, and scientific findings into interactive storytelling adventures.

The platform explores five remarkable spacecraft: Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Ingenuity, InSight, and Pioneer 10. Each chapter combines historical storytelling with engaging scientific activities, allowing players to investigate real discoveries and understand the engineering challenges behind space exploration.

Through explorer profiles, experience points (XP), achievements, and a Discovery Journal, NovaExplorer makes learning about space more engaging and rewarding.

Our goal is to preserve the legacies of these extraordinary machines while inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers.

NovaExplorer — Project DetailsOverview

https://github.com/mchithna/NASASpaceApps

NovaExplorer is an interactive, gamified educational platform created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the "Abandoned But Not Forgotten" challenge.

The project aims to preserve and communicate the remarkable scientific and engineering legacies of retired NASA spacecraft through engaging, story-driven experiences.

Traditional mission archives contain valuable scientific information, but younger audiences may find it difficult to connect with technical records and historical descriptions. NovaExplorer addresses this by transforming authentic NASA mission information into accessible, interactive adventures.

How It Works

Players enter NovaExplorer through a futuristic Mission Control interface and create an explorer profile or continue as guests.

They can select from five standalone spacecraft chapters:

1. Surveyor 3 — The Robot They Came Back For

Players investigate the lunar lander's unusual landing, examine its soil experiments, and uncover why Apollo 12 astronauts returned to retrieve components from it.

2. Opportunity — The Explorer That Wouldn't Stop

Players follow the rover's extraordinary journey across Mars, investigate geological evidence of ancient water, explore navigation challenges, and discover how a major dust storm brought the mission to an end.

3. Ingenuity — Five Flights Became Seventy-Two

Players discover how NASA achieved powered flight on another planet and explore the engineering challenges and accomplishments of the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter.

4. InSight — The Machine That Listened to Mars

Players investigate seismic signals, distinguish marsquakes from environmental noise, and discover how scientists studied Mars's crust, mantle, and core.

5. Pioneer 10 — The Messenger That Never Came Home

Players explore the spacecraft's journey past Jupiter, the challenges of deep-space communication, and the message carried by the Pioneer plaque.

Each mission combines narrative scenes, NASA-supported scientific information, and interactive learning activities.

The platform incorporates a gamification system where players earn XP, advance through explorer ranks, unlock mission achievements, and preserve their scientific findings in a personal Discovery Journal.

Technology and Development

NovaExplorer was developed as a web application using:

  • React and TypeScript for the interactive frontend.
  • Vite for the development and build environment.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive styling and a consistent design system.
  • React Router for navigation and mission progression.
  • Supabase Authentication and PostgreSQL for explorer accounts, saved progress, achievements, and XP records.
  • HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG-based interfaces for interactive activities and scientific visualizations.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.

A reusable mission engine provides shared functionality for scene navigation, interactive activity completion, checkpoints, rewards, and chapter progression, while allowing each spacecraft to have its own story and unique educational activities.

No specialized physical hardware is required. The platform is designed to run in a modern web browser.

NASA Resources and Scientific Accuracy

NovaExplorer draws on NASA's published mission histories, scientific findings, photographs, instrument descriptions, and available observation records.

These resources help us present accurate historical events and develop educational activities inspired by genuine scientific investigations.

The project distinguishes real mission observations from simplified simulations. Interactive exercises are designed to explain scientific principles rather than reproduce actual spacecraft operations or telemetry.

NASA resources are acknowledged through mission references and source credits.

Creativity and Innovation

NovaExplorer combines three concepts: interactive storytelling, scientific investigation, and game-based learning.

Instead of offering a collection of static articles or repetitive quizzes, each spacecraft chapter presents a distinct experience based on its actual mission.

The platform also connects these independent stories through a shared progression system, allowing players to grow from Space Cadets into more experienced explorers.

Our central creative idea is that a spacecraft's story should not end when its communication stops. Its discoveries and scientific legacy can continue inspiring people long afterward.

Intended Impact

NovaExplorer is designed primarily for school-age students and young space enthusiasts.

We aim to make space science easier to understand, encourage curiosity about engineering and planetary exploration, and help younger audiences appreciate the scientific value of historic NASA missions.

The platform could also support classroom learning, science outreach, and informal STEM education.

In the future, NovaExplorer could expand to include additional retired spacecraft, more interactive scientific investigations, and educational resources for teachers.

Their missions ended. Their stories didn't.
